speaker: SPEAKER_01
transcript: From our nation's capital, this is Napschat. Hi and welcome to the first episode of Nat's Chat for the year 2021. I'm Bob Levy, the Director of Legislative and Political Affairs for the National Association of Postal Supervisors. A lot has happened since Nat's Chat took a one-week hiatus. Most prominent were acts of insurrection waged on Wednesday by a presidentially inspired mob who desecrated the U.S. Capitol, America's holy temple of our Democratic Republic. Those who incited or committed sedition failed to stop our elected representatives from conducting the people's business and certifying the tabulation of the 2020 Electoral College. Later on this podcast, I will host one of the congressional heroes of that day, Representative Jason Crow of Colorado, who helped secure the House of Representatives Chamber and helped to protect and offer comfort to his congressional colleagues. In fact, Republican House leader Kevin McCarthy identified Representative Crow when the House was able to reconvene as one of the heroes of the day. My conversation with Representative Crow preceded the events of the insurrection, so there is no reference to it in the podcast. Also this week, voters in Georgia elected Reverend Rafael Warnock and John Ossoff, both Democrats as U.S. senators. With the election and with Vice President Harris being the Senate's presiding officer, the Democratic Party assumes majority status in the Senate. For NAP's members in the postal community, this means that Senator Gary Peters of Michigan will succeed Senator Ron Johnson as Chairman of the Senate Homeland Security and Government Affairs Committee. This has brought implications for the Postal Service as the President will be able to nominate four new members to the Postal Service Board of Governors to fill the current vacancies. Also, there have been more mundane issues these past two weeks. After considerable unnecessary White House drama, President Trump grudgingly signed the year-end pandemic relief bill, which included a provision converting a Postal Service $10 billion line of credit into a grant to the Postal Service for coronavirus-related expenses. Although this aid is far less than that called for in legislation previously passed by the House of Representatives, it is naps' hope that postal leadership will put the $10 billion to good use. Appended to the coronavirus bill was an omnibus appropriation bill that funds the federal government through September 31, 2021. In addition, the Postal Board of Governors announced that it intended to use its new rate-setting authority granted by the Postal Regulatory Commission to adjust rates to take into account the increased cost of providing mail delivery to each delivery point as the result of a shrinking mail volume. and to adjust rates to account for postal retirement and amortization payments. Let's now turn to this week's NAPS chat. I'm honored to greet as our guest, Congressman Jason Crow, who represents the area of Colorado to the east of Denver, which includes the community of Aurora, Centennial, and Littleton. Congressman Crow is just sworn in for his second term as a member of the House and has served as a member of the House Armed Services Committee and the House Committee on Small Business. As a member of Congress, Representative Crow has established a strong relationship with NAP's legislative advocate, Gary Raul, and has been a leader in defending postal employees as well as the agency from political attacks and political interference. Congressman Crow, welcome to NAP's chat and congratulations on your second swearing-in this week.
